investigation: Gamow-Teller Resonance and Effective Axial-Vector Coupling g_A Quenching across Mass Regions
description: Systematic evaluation of g_A quenching from light p-shell nuclei (6He) to heavy doubly magic systems (100Sn, 208Pb) and double-beta emitters (76Ge, 130Te, 136Xe), demonstrating the monotonic mass scaling q(A) and refuting the naive transfer of low-momentum 2nu quenching to 0nu beta beta.

boundary_1_mass_dependent_core_polarizat.contrast: Light nuclei (6He, q=0.88) vs Heavy nuclei (208Pb, q=0.68)
boundary_1_mass_dependent_core_polarizat.mechanism: In light nuclei, the compact single-particle space and large shell gaps severely restrict the number of virtual 2p-2h tensor doorways within the 50 MeV continuum, keeping quenching mild (q ~ 0.88). In heavy nuclei (A >= 100), the dense Fermi sea maximizes tensor force second-order mixing, dispersing 30-32% of the Ikeda sum rule into the high-energy continuum (20-50 MeV), as confirmed by RCNP (3He,t) reactions. A single universal quenching factor across all mass regions is invalid.
boundary_1_mass_dependent_core_polarizat.failure_signature: Overestimating beta-decay rates in heavy nuclei when using p-shell or sd-shell effective g_A values.

boundary_2_momentum_transfer_inapplicabi.contrast: Allowed 2nu beta beta (q ~ 0) vs Virtual Majorana 0nu beta beta (q ~ 150 MeV/c)
boundary_2_momentum_transfer_inapplicabi.mechanism: 2nu beta beta proceeds through intermediate 1+ GT states at zero momentum transfer, experiencing full 2p-2h core polarization quenching (q^4 ~ 0.24). 0nu beta beta is mediated by a virtual neutrino propagator H(r) ~ 1/r with average momentum transfer q ~ 150 MeV/c. Over 85% of the transition is carried by higher-order multipoles (J^pi = 2-, 3+, 4-, 5+), which do not couple to the Gamow-Teller giant resonance and suffer negligible quenching (q_0nu ~ 0.95, q^4 ~ 0.83). Naively applying 2nu quenching to 0nu beta beta artificially depresses the matrix element by a factor of ~3.5.
boundary_2_momentum_transfer_inapplicabi.failure_signature: Severe underestimation of 0nu beta beta half-life sensitivity by factor of 3 to 4 in GERDA, KamLAND-Zen, and LEGEND analyses.
